notes.status: Qualification (layout parity, loop order, 150-schedule replay pilot, noise) is recorded under data/nano/qualification; collection remains gated: schedule_rules and postprocessors stay null until the collection gate is explicitly opened.
notes.compiler: M2 TVM LLVM emits AArch64 code; Nano-side RPC archive linking invoked /usr/bin/g++.
notes.num_cores: 4 online Cortex-A57 cores (lscpu on the Nano); one cpufreq policy spans CPUs 0-3.
notes.cache: L1D 32 KiB per core (cpu0/cache/index0: level 1, Data, 32K, shared_cpu_list 0) and L2 2 MiB shared (index2: level 2, Unified, 2048K, shared_cpu_list 0-3), read from sysfs and lscpu on the Nano.
notes.simd: AArch64 Advanced SIMD ('asimd' in /proc/cpuinfo): 128-bit vectors = 4 FP32 lanes and 32 architectural V registers (V0-V31). Cross-compiled schedules emit fmla v.4s (j3 >= 4) and fmla v.2s (j3 = 2).
notes.peak_flops: initial guess, fitted on TRAIN only: 4 cores x 1.479e9 Hz (cpuinfo_max_freq) x 8 FP32 FLOP/cycle (one 128-bit FMLA per cycle per core). scripts/nano_fma_peak.c measured 11.80 GFLOP/s on one core (7.98 FLOP/cycle) and 46.5 GFLOP/s on four cores at 1479 MHz, so this is an attainable FMA ceiling, not a matmul throughput or a specification.
notes.bandwidth_bytes_s: initial guess, fitted on TRAIN only: ~1e10 B/s, rounded from the 4-thread parallel-vector test (2 x 16 MiB read+write in 3.090 ms = 1.09e10 B/s; results/jetson_nano/validate_threading_4t_configured.json); not a specification.
